text:
olivia: follow-up from RFC thread 7:007
	

quick note: teams keep asking for mid-chat precision downgrade (fp8 -> int8/4bit) to save compute when chat becomes cheap. main Qs: data compatibility, user-visible regressions, billing semantics, and rollout ops.

raj: summary: feasible but several surfaces. parity issues: packing/layout, scale/zp, and op-level ordering. also need to decide whether we allow mixture in GPU register allocation.

marco: engineering options (ranked by simplicity -> complexity):
- fallback-reencode: on switch, synchronous re-quantize KV to target precision (simple correctness, latency spike).
- shadow-requant: start background job to generate target cache while serving from old cache; switch when ready (best UX).
- ephemeral dual-cache: keep both encodings for "hot" convos only (fast switch, memory cost).
- canonical intermediate: store a compact fp16 canonical and quantize on-demand (balanced).

chen: we need to measure two things: 1) correctness delta (top-k divergence + degscore) and 2) cost model (memory vs cpu convert vs per-token saved GPU FLOP). i'll own experiments.

maya: billing/legal note: if we route a request mid-chat to a cheaper precision, are we allowed to charge lower price retroactively? need product/finance input. provisional rule: charges are per-response precision. but for refunds/credits we might need a policy.

lisa: ops implications: migration for existing persisted caches: add header + schema version. create a backfill job. also, metrics to monitor: "precision_switch_failures", "requant_latency_ms", "degscore_tail_99p". plan a staged rollout: shadow -> canary 1% -> 10% -> global.

olivia: on compatibility metadata, propose fields: version, model_name, layer_idx, seq_len, bitwidth, quant_param_hash, op_tag, created_ts. keep header < 64 bytes.

raj: runtime decision matrix sketch: if exact match bitwidth+op_tag -> fast path; else if customer kvcache_compat=best-effort -> try best-effort (feed through dequant->requant pipeline) and mark request with trace flag; else reject with 409 or force re-encode.

marco: perf heuristic: only create dual cache if convo_active_time > X or expected remaining tokens > Y. we can approximate remaining tokens from recent rates. default: X=60s, Y=128 tokens.

chen: experiment plan (short): sample 5k real prefixes across retrieval-heavy and open-chat; switch at token 8/16/32; collect top1 change rate, PPL delta, degscore, and worst-case burst cases. baseline: fp8 -> int4 and fp8 -> int8.

olivia: quick local run shows fp8->int4 median top1-prob L1=0.09, 95p=0.6, degscore median 0.02. not ideal for retrieval-heavy.

maya: product ask: expose API param: "allow_precision_switch": true|false per-session; default false for legacy customers. will require acceptance in TOS for charging model.

lisa: ops action items: docs, migration job, canary plan, playbook for rollback. need to schedule DB migration window; ops-bot, please remind infra team when canary starts.

raj: dev action items:
- header spec draft (me)
- runtime switcher state machine (fast/fallback)
- background requant worker prototype (marco + ben)

chen: eval action items:
- experiment harness + dataset selection
- metrics dashboard + alert rules

maya: product action items:
- pricing guidance on per-response precision and customer-facing controls
- opt-in policy for beta customers

ops-bot: :calendar: canary window scheduled 2026-04-02 08:00 UTC -> 2026-04-09 08:00 UTC (shadow preceding 2w)

marco: small engineering note: we must include op_impl and kernel_version in header to avoid subtle mismatch across runtime releases. also consider checksum of serialized block to detect corruption.

olivia: OK let's try shadow for 2 weeks, chen will start experiments tomorrow, raj + marco to ship header+worker prototype this sprint. will reconvene after initial telemetry.

maya: ping finance on billing semantics thread pls.

lisa: thanks everyone. filing this into RFC follow-ups board. :white_check_mark:
